title: Stream resynthesis tool for event-time-aware metric reprocessing
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: We need a safe, repeatable system to reprocess historical console usage events (API calls, model selection, billing labels) such that downstream derived metrics (per-route latency percentiles, cost per token aggregates, active-route counts) can be corrected when we change enrichment logic, schema mappings, or fix bugs. Current ad-hoc backfills are error-prone, cause duplicated counts, and lack observability for partial failures.

Goal: Build a Stream Resynthesis Tool (SRT) that reads archived event batches and live topic partitions, replays events into the analytics pipeline with event-time semantics, enforces idempotency, and trims or replays tombstones to correctly handle deletions. The tool must support incremental reprocessing windows, schema evolution, and produce artifacts suitable for re-materializing materialized views and downstream dashboards without manual SQL surgery.
acceptance_criteria: SRT can consume a time-range of archived events and replay them into the enrichment layer with preserved event_time and original partitioning key
Replayed events are idempotent: downstream aggregates remain stable if the same event range is replayed multiple times
Tool supports a dry-run mode that produces a diff preview (expected row-level changes) without applying writes
SRT provides per-batch observability: records processed, ingested, dropped, dupes detected, and wall-clock vs event-time skew
Schema drift is handled: unmapped fields are captured to an audit table and processing continues with the latest mapping rules
Reprocessing of deletions tombstones results in consistent downstream state (no ghost rows remain)
SRT integrates with Console rollouts: can be triggered from the web UI and exposes progress and rollback hooks
design_notes: Use Kafka topics for replay but implement an abstraction so archived S3 objects or GCS bundles can be streamed without changing downstream consumers
Event-time watermarking will be applied; use bounded-lateness policy (configurable) to drop extremely late events or route them to a review queue
Implement idempotency via a composite dedupe key (event_id + original_source_offset + model_version_tag) and a short-lived dedupe store in DynamoDB/Redis
For schema evolution, maintain a registry of mapping rules in the config service; unknown fields persisted to an audit prefix in the parquet archive
Provide a materialized-view repair job runner that can automatically recompute SQL-driven aggregates for named dashboards after replay completes
implementation_tasks: Prototype a replay client that reads archived S3 event bundles and streams them to Kafka with original event_time headers
Add idempotency middleware to enrichment service to accept dedupe headers and perform upserts to analytics write topics
Implement dry-run mode that computes expected deltas using a shadow Kafka topic and stores diffs in an artifacts bucket
Create an operator CLI and console job endpoint to schedule replays, with options: time-range, batch-size, watermark-lateness, dry-run
Add observability: Prometheus metrics for replay throughput, Sentry alerts for fatal decode/schema errors, and a replay dashboard in Grafana
Write end-to-end tests that inject synthetic late events, tombstones, and duplicated batches to validate idempotency and deletion handling
Document runbooks for failed partial replays and rollback procedures for materialized view corrections
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with Analytics, Runtime, and Console teams. Agreed on SRT scope and risk bounds.
2026-02-18: Prototype replay client MVP can stream a single S3 bundle to the dev Kafka topic preserving event_time headers
2026-02-24: Implemented dedupe key scheme and small Redis-based dedupe store. Verified basic idempotency with unit tests
2026-02-28: Dry-run shadow topic completed; initial diff artifact format (parquet) defined. Began work on Grafana replay dashboard

2026-03-02: Discovered an edge case where tombstone ordering with Kafka compaction leads to transient duplicates in the enrichment joins. Added plan to use compacted tombstone topic and per-key sequence numbers to ensure monotonic deletes
risks: Long-running replays may overload enrichment workers; need adaptive rate limiting and back-pressure to avoid SLA regressions
Idempotency store scale: reprocessing large date ranges could create hot keys in Redis/Dynamo; require sharding strategy and TTLs
Schema drift could cause data loss if unmapped fields contain critical info; audit pipeline must be durable and monitored
Cost: reading terabytes from object storage and writing to Kafka will incur noticeable egress and compute costs—must estimate before large runs
Operational complexity for partial failures where only some partitions completed; need clear retry semantics
qa_plan: Unit tests for replay client, dedupe middleware, and mapping registry
Integration test against staging Kafka + enrichment service that validates end-to-end aggregates against a golden dataset
Chaos test: inject duplicate bundles, out-of-order tombstones, and network time skew to validate robustness
Performance benchmark: measure replays/sec and downstream CPU/RAM impacts for a 7-day historic window
deploy_plan: Deploy replay client as a k8s job in staging with canary rate limit at 5% of expected production throughput
Run a dry-run for a non-critical 48-hour window and validate diffs in the artifacts bucket
Schedule a controlled full-run during off-peak hours with monitoring runbooks and pager duty pre-notification
Post-replay: run materialized view repair job and validate dashboards; if drift > threshold, trigger rollback and alert stakeholders
